description: Cluster 1: Consumers’ attitude towards collection-and-delivery points. This cluster comprises papers that examine the adoption of collection-and-delivery points from the perspective of customers. These papers are anchored on several consumer theories, such as innovation diffusion theory (IDT) or the technology acceptance model (TAM), to build models with hypotheses that are subsequently tested by using structural equation modelling. The favourable attitude of consumers is a key determinant of their adoption of CDP services. Consumers’ attitudes significantly affect the acceptance of delivery methods, which could be explained in terms of perceived relative advantage (Chen et  al., 2018; Wang et  al., 2018, 2020; Yuen et  al., 2018) and perceived sustainability (Klein & Popp, 2022; Milioti et  al., 2020). In other words, consumers will be highly likely to use CDP services if they can provide value to individuals and society.

Cluster 2: Parcel lockers as a self-service technology. With the disruption of the COVID-19 pandemic, a large number of consumers have embraced self-service technologies to fulfill their daily needs (Wang, Wong, et  al., 2021). The second cluster revolves around parcel locker usage intention, which can be seen as an effective and efficient solution of self-service technologies for e-commerce last-mile delivery (Tsai & Tiwasing, 2021). From the perspective of technology, the benefits brought by logistics technologies are key driving factors in consumers’ usage behaviour of parcel lockers. These can be explained in terms of technology service convenience with consumer participation readiness theory/resource matching theory (Chen et  al., 2020; Jiang et  al., 2023; Yuen et  al., 2019) or technology acceptance factors with TAM/UTAUT theory (Cai et  al., 2021). In the context of the COVID-19 pandemic, consumers are increasingly reliant on technology where technological innovativeness and health concerns motivate consumers’ parcel-locker usage behaviour (Wang, Wong, et  al., 2021; Wang et  al., 2022)

Cluster 3: Co-creating logistics service value. Cluster 3 classifies research on consumer participation behaviour in co-creating logistics service values. Different from the view of being beneficiaries of using last-mile delivery innovation, like automated parcel stations, which have been examined by studies in the previous two clusters, the focus on this cluster has shifted to the development of co-creating logistics services where consumers have the right to organise their logistics operations. By using structural equation modelling (SEM), these papers have found critical factors when encouraging consumers to participate in last-mile logistics services, the collection-and-delivery points in particular, which are enjoyable experiences (Wang et  al., 2019), security (Risher et  al., 2020), and fairness (Wang, Yuen, et  al., 2021). Table 5 summarises the findings of the bibliographic coupling analysis. Three research fronts have been identified within the field of CDPs: consumers’ attitudes, self-service technology, and co-creating logistics service value
